candidates.explanation: I believe resetPassword only verifies the JWT hash (signature and expiry) and then sets the new password. It does not invalidate the token afterwards. Nothing ties the token to the current password state, such as a password-hash fingerprint or a stored one-time token, and nothing marks it as used.

I believe forgotPassword signs a stateless JWT containing only forgotUserId. It has no nonce, no jti, and no password-version claim, and nothing is stored server-side. That makes single-use enforcement impossible when the token is verified later.

fix.description: Make the reset token single-use. In forgotPassword, include a fingerprint of the user's current password hash in the JWT payload, for example a hash of user.password. In resetPassword, load the user and reject the token with a 422 if the fingerprint no longer matches the current password, or if the stored token is missing or already used. After the password is updated, clear or consume the token. The password change then invalidates the old link automatically.
